references.text: God warns Israel against making a covenant with those who live in the land they are about to enter, a direct parallel to the prohibition in Exodus 23:32.
Repeats the warning against making a covenant with the inhabitants of the land and their gods, focusing on the danger of idolatry.
Moses repeats the prohibition against making a covenant with the Canaanite peoples when Israel is about to take possession of the land.
The Israelites express concern about making a covenant with the Hivites, showing that they were aware of the prohibition against such covenants.
Joshua warns the people not to make a covenant with the remaining nations in the land, in line with God's original command.
The angel of the Lord reminds Israel that they were not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, a command they had broken.
Warns against serving the gods of other peoples, which is connected to the prohibition against making covenants with them.
Joshua 23:7 specifies and applies the prohibition against covenants with foreign gods given in Exodus 23:32.
Psalm 81:10 expresses the theological consequence of not making a covenant with foreign gods: complete exclusivity for the Lord.
Deuteronomy 6:14 expands and confirms the prohibition against following other gods given in Exodus 23:32.
2 Kings 17:35 shows historically how breaking the covenant and the prohibition against other gods from Exodus led to God's judgment.
Exodus 23:24 is the direct practical consequence of the prohibition in Exodus 23:32: destruction of the cultic sites to break all alliances.
